# Riverbend Nonprofit Network theory of change: who does what

## Division of labour

| Actor | Roles | Delivers | Changes or co-owns | Runs |
|-------|-------|----------|--------------------|------|
| Riverbend Nonprofit Network (`act-network`) | Implementer, champion | Residents get timely, good-quality services from local nonprofits | — | Run mixed-size peer-learning cohorts; Offer one-to-one leadership coaching; Run pooled bookkeeping and payroll help; Negotiate group purchasing agreements; Maintain a shared grants calendar; Publish plain-language policy briefings; Convene member forums to draft joint positions |
| Small member nonprofits (`act-members-small`) | Beneficiary, adopter | Residents get timely, good-quality services from local nonprofits | Member nonprofits run strong, well-managed organizations; Members routinely collaborate instead of duplicating effort; Members have diversified, stable funding; Member leaders apply improved management practices; Members turn to each other for advice and joint work; Members spend less staff time and money on back-office work; Members apply for more grants that fit their mission; Members adopt and share joint positions on local issues; Leaders gain coaching-based skills and confidence; Members form peer relationships across sizes; Members use pooled back-office services; Members consult the shared grants calendar when planning; Members understand local policy and funding processes | — |
| Larger member nonprofits (`act-members-large`) | Boundary partner, influencer | Residents get timely, good-quality services from local nonprofits | Member nonprofits run strong, well-managed organizations; Members routinely collaborate instead of duplicating effort; Member leaders apply improved management practices; Members turn to each other for advice and joint work; Members adopt and share joint positions on local issues; Leaders gain coaching-based skills and confidence; Members form peer relationships across sizes; Members understand local policy and funding processes | — |
| Riverbend County Office of Community Planning (`act-county-office`) | Gatekeeper, boundary partner | Local officials and funders engage members in planning | Local government and funders consult members through a coordinated channel; Local officials and funders engage members in planning; A standing channel exists between members and the county planning office | Set up a standing liaison channel with the county planning office |
| Millbrook Town Council (`act-city-council`) | Gatekeeper | Local officials and funders engage members in planning | Local government and funders consult members through a coordinated channel; Local officials and funders engage members in planning | — |
| Lowland Regional Fund (`act-regional-funder`) | Funder, influencer | — | Local government and funders consult members through a coordinated channel; Members apply for more grants that fit their mission; Local officials and funders engage members in planning | Host a funder and member roundtable |
| Riverbend County Library System (`act-library`) | Boundary partner, champion | — | — | — |
| Northfield Learning Studio (`act-training-partner`) | Implementer | — | — | Deliver a management skills training series |
| Pooled-service vendors (`act-vendors`) | Adopter | — | — | — |
| Residents of Riverbend County (`act-residents`) | Beneficiary | — | Residents get timely, good-quality services from local nonprofits; Residents' priorities shape local public decisions | — |
| Network board of directors (`act-board`) | Gatekeeper, champion | — | — | — |

## Outcomes that need collaboration

- Residents get timely, good-quality services from local nonprofits (`oc-resident-access`), shared: Riverbend Nonprofit Network, Small member nonprofits, Larger member nonprofits
- Local officials and funders engage members in planning (`oc-im-officials-engage`), partner: Riverbend County Office of Community Planning, Millbrook Town Council

## Outcomes with no one delivering them

- Member nonprofits run strong, well-managed organizations (`oc-lt-capable-members`)
- Members routinely collaborate instead of duplicating effort (`oc-lt-collab`)
- Members have diversified, stable funding (`oc-lt-sustainable`)
- Local government and funders consult members through a coordinated channel (`oc-lt-collective-voice`)
- Member leaders apply improved management practices (`oc-im-leaders-practice`)
- Members turn to each other for advice and joint work (`oc-im-peer-network`)
- Members spend less staff time and money on back-office work (`oc-im-lower-overhead`)
- Members apply for more grants that fit their mission (`oc-im-grant-pipeline`)

## Outcomes partners deliver, which are monitored

| Outcome | Delivered by | Measured by | Status |
|---------|--------------|-------------|--------|
| Local officials and funders engage members in planning (`oc-im-officials-engage`) | Riverbend County Office of Community Planning, Millbrook Town Council | ind-officials-meetings | At risk |
